I need to get a clear picture of how the core generation and interactive logic works in this project so I can design the new “Teich Studio” UI and command entry point. The user wants a CLI entry `teich studio` that launches a browser UI, and also an interactive mode that spins up a Docker container and lets the user steer a conversation session. To implement that, I’ll have to hook into the existing runner infrastructure, which already knows how to launch various model runners (ChatRunner, ClaudeCodeRunner, etc.) and handle session progress updates.

So far I have listed the repository contents, read the README, and inspected a few key source files: `cli.py`, `config.py`, and I noted the size of `runner.py` (5,574 lines) which suggests it contains a lot of logic. To plan the integration, I need to understand the high‑level structure of `runner.py`: what classes are defined, what key functions exist, and where the entry points for running a generation or starting an interactive session are located. This will tell me where to add a new command in the Typer CLI, and how to invoke the existing runners from the UI backend.

A good way to get that overview without reading the entire 5k‑line file is to extract the definitions of classes and functions. I can grep for lines starting with `class` or `def`, and also include indented `def` lines to capture methods inside classes. Limiting the output to the first 120 matches will give me a manageable outline of the file’s structure.

Therefore, I will run a grep command on `src/teich/runner.py` that searches for lines beginning with `class ` or `def `, as well as lines that have the typical indentation for method definitions (`    def `). I’ll pipe that through `head -120` to keep the result concise. This will provide the skeleton of the runner module, which I can then use to decide where to hook the new Studio functionality.
